name: BEN (C-Worker 4)
notes: BEN, the Bathymetric Explorer and Navigator: an ASV Global C-Worker 4 built in 2016, the 4 m ASV this console models (Andy, 2026-10-10: 'It is to be used as the 4m ASV in your current vessel file'). A Yanmar 3YM30AE diesel through a centrifugal clutch, direct drive to a waterjet, with a Kongsberg EM2040P on a ram amidships. MEASURED off ASV Global's general arrangement ASV-396-7-000-i0001-01-C, rev C, 08/03/2016 (embedded in 'BEN Calibration and Offsets Narrative for BEN_v1.0', UNH CCOM, 2018): length, hull draft, and the side areas above and below the waterline. Andy's own figures: 5.5 kn through the water, surveying at full throttle, for 20 h, and a 100 L tank. The beam is the C-Worker 4 sheet's. ESTIMATED, not measured: the front wind area, the turn rate, the loiter speed, the under-keel clearance, the buffer, the maneuvering and autopilot numbers, and the fuel burn below full throttle (see the fuel block's source). Until 2026-10-10 this place was held by example_usv_4m, an illustrative hull with a battery.

hull.wind_source: SIDE MEASURED OFF THE GA (2026-10-10): the drawing's 1700 mm dimension scales it at 2.562 mm/px, and it reproduces the drawing's own 404 mm and 630 mm vertical dimensions to 0.4%. The vessel's outer silhouette above the waterline - hull, deckhouse, mast, radome, antennas and camera - is 3.46 m^2 (the mast, radome, antennas and camera 0.27 of it); overall 4.21 m from the jet guard to the bow, 3.90 m on the waterline, the antenna tops 1.97 m above water. FRONT ESTIMATED, 1.7 m^2 (1.5-1.9): no front view is drawn. The hull's face, the published 1.6 m beam x 0.69 m freeboard at the forward deck less a tenth for the topsides' shape, about 0.99; the deckhouse, 0.39 m proud of that deck at an assumed 1.2 m wide, about 0.47; the superstructure about 0.27. above_water_h_m is the side area / length, used only where these areas are absent.
hull.underwater_source: MEASURED OFF THE SAME GA: the silhouette from the waterline to the hull bottom (the drawing's 404 mm line) - hull, skeg, and the waterjet and its guard - is 1.39 m^2. The drawing's 2016 sidescan, below the hull, is not BEN today and is left out. The EM2040P's pod adds area when the ram lowers it; it is left out too, because the smaller area gives the larger leeway.
hull.draft_source: 0.66 m is the deepest point while SURVEYING - the EM2040P's face with the ram extended - not the hull: the 2018 offsets diagram in that UNH CCOM narrative puts it 0.659 m below the waterline extended and 0.359 m retracted (a 300 mm stroke), and says the sonar is normally run extended (Andy, 2026-10-10: 'use the 2018 offsets, 0.66 m'). The hull alone draws 0.404 m (the GA). It was 1.3 m for the day this file was written, from an August figure of 0.9 m below the hull that the offsets diagram does not bear out.

propulsion.source: Andy, 2026-08-26: 5.5 kn through the water is her top speed, and 'BEN surveys at full throttle usually', so survey = high = 5.5 kn (the C-Worker 4 sheet's 'up to 9 knots' is not this boat). Selectable in whole knots, 2 to 5. low 2.0 kn is ESTIMATED (WorldView's loiter figure).

fuel.source: TANK 100 L: Andy, 2026-10-10 ('BENS fuel tank size is 100 liters'). FULL BURN 5.0 L/h DERIVED from his two figures, the 100 L and 20 h of survey at full throttle (5.5 kn), on the reading that the 20 h runs the tank dry; a full tank is then 20 h and 110 nm at survey speed. If the 20 h kept a reserve, the true burn is lower. The idle burn (1.0 L/h) and the exponent (3, power against speed) are still GUESSES - replace them with her measured burn when there is one.
